metaDescription: Six 60 pint class dehumidifiers compared on honest ratings, tank size, noise, drainage and coverage for large basements and whole-level use.
expertTake: The Frigidaire 60 pint is the pick for buyers who want a plain, major-brand machine with a continuous drain option. The Ludatido is the value pick for a big tank and a quiet floor. Skip this size for anything smaller than a large open lower level, because a 60 pint compressor in a small room short-cycles and wears out sooner.
introParagraphs: Sixty pints is where a dehumidifier stops being an appliance for one room and becomes a machine for a whole level. These units are heavy, they draw real power, and they only make sense where the moisture load is large enough to keep them running for hours at a stretch.

That also makes the fine print more important. Sellers at this size love to print a maximum figure from a hot, saturated lab test next to a modest honest number, and the gap between them can be a third or more. This guide sorts the lineup by what each model really claims.

products.name: Frigidaire 60 Pint Dehumidifier with Continuous Drain
products.description:
This Frigidaire is a conventional refrigerant-coil machine in the largest size the maker sells for homes. Its feature list is short and sensible: a washable filter that keeps dust off the coil, a custom humidity control, and a continuous drain option so you can skip the bucket. For a whole-level problem, those basics are what you want from a machine that will run most of the day.

The tradeoff is that it offers less than the newer brands on paper. It does not publish a decibel figure, an efficiency number or a long list of modes, and it sits at the highest price tier in the lineup. You pay for the brand name, for filters you can find years from now, and for a service network that outlasts a typical marketplace seller.

Plan on a hose to a floor drain, because a 60 pint machine fills a bucket quickly in a damp room. Wash the filter monthly, wipe the tank, and leave a foot of clearance around the intake. In year three the wear points are the fan motor and the bucket float, and both are cheap to service on a major-brand body. Sit it on a low platform if your drain is only slightly lower than the floor.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a major-brand 60 pint unit with a continuous drain and easy parts.
pros: Major brand with easy filters and service
Continuous drain option for hands-free use
Custom humidity setting is simple to use
cons: Highest price tier in the lineup
No published noise or efficiency figures

products.name: Ludatido 80 Pint Dehumidifier 5,000 sq ft with 1.72 gal Tank
products.description:
Ludatido sells an 80 pint maximum figure, which is a hot-lab peak, so the realistic output sits well below it, likely in the same neighborhood as a 60 pint rating on the current test. What it adds is a 1.72 gallon tank with auto shutoff and a stated minimum noise of 42 dB. That combination is aimed at buyers who dislike emptying and who want to run it near living space.

The larger tank is the more practical benefit. A 60 pint class machine in a damp basement can fill a small bucket in under a day, and a bigger one buys you a margin on days you cannot get downstairs. The lower price tier compared with the Frigidaire reflects a newer brand without the service network.

Keep the receipt, register the product and treat the 42 dB as a minimum-speed reading. A hose to a floor drain removes the tank question entirely. Remember that a full 1.72 gallon tank weighs about 14 pounds of water alone, so use the handle with both hands and empty it before carrying the machine anywhere.
products.bestFor: Large basements where you want a big tank and a quiet floor at a lower price tier.
pros: Lower price tier than the major brand
cons: 80 pint figure is a hot-lab peak
Newer brand with less service reach

products.name: ARLIME 60 Pint Dehumidifier 4,000 sq ft with 6.5L Tank
products.description:
ARLIME is unusually candid: the listing gives 60 pints at 95F and 90 percent humidity and a lower 45 pint figure under a milder test. That second number is the one to plan around, and it tells you the 60 label belongs to a hot, saturated room. A seller who prints both figures is giving you the information you need to size the machine properly.

It offers three modes, auto, continuous drying and sleep, with two fan speeds, and a 6.5 liter tank that is a little over 1.7 gallons. At a mid price tier it sits between the Ludatido and the Frigidaire. The coverage claim is 4,000 square feet, more modest than the rivals.

For a damp basement, run it in continuous mode for the first few days and then drop back to auto. Clean the filter on schedule and verify the humidity with a separate meter. Because the sleep mode lowers fan speed, it also lowers output, so use it overnight only after the room has already dropped to your target.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want clear rating information and a mid price tier.
pros: Lists both a hot and a milder pint rating
6.5 liter tank with a flexible drain

products.name: WATTSMART 60 Pint Dehumidifier 6,500 sq ft with Hose
products.description:
WATTSMART claims 6,500 square feet, the biggest coverage figure in this lineup, and offers three modes with a 30 to 80 percent target range. The listing calls out an efficient, energy-saving compressor design and three drainage options, including a carry handle for emptying the tank. The 60 pint number is described as a maximum, so treat it as the best case.

The coverage claim looks large because it assumes a mild moisture load. In a wet basement, a unit rated like this will cover far less. It sits at a mid price tier, above the Ludatido but below the Frigidaire.

Use the hose option for continuous drain, support it so it cannot kink, and check the line each season. Do not buy it for the square footage alone. Match the claim to your room by assuming only about half of it applies if the space is wet.
products.bestFor: Large open spaces with a mild moisture problem and a drain nearby.
pros: Largest coverage claim in the lineup
cons: Pint figure stated as a maximum

products.name: GarveeLife 57 Pint Dehumidifier 3,000 sq ft Energy Star
products.description:
GarveeLife is the lowest price tier here, an Energy Star certified compressor unit with three fan speeds, a 30 to 80 percent target range and a programmable timer. The title says 57 pints while the description calls it a 60 pint unit, a small inconsistency that reinforces the advice to read the label carefully. Auto shutoff protects the floor.

It is rated for 3,000 square feet, which puts it at the small end of the 60 pint class. For a finished basement of that size, it is a sensible, low-cost choice. For a larger or wetter space, the Ludatido or Frigidaire gives more margin.

Wash the filter on schedule and give the machine room to exhaust warm air. The programmable timer lets you run the machine only during off-peak electricity hours, which can lower running cost.
products.bestFor: Medium basements and budget buyers who want Energy Star certification.
pros: Lowest price tier in the lineup
Three fan speeds and a timer
cons: Title and description disagree on pints

products.name: Midea 60 Pint Dehumidifier with Pump 5,500 sq ft
products.description:
The Midea is the pump option in this lineup, with three drainage choices, a built-in pump that moves water vertically or horizontally, and a hose in the box. Wi-Fi control lets you adjust it from upstairs. It claims 5,500 square feet.

A pump matters when the drain is higher than the machine, as in many below-grade basements. It adds cost, so it sits near the top of the price tier. If a floor drain is beside the machine, a simpler hose model is cheaper.

Flush the pump line each season and keep the hose from kinking. The Wi-Fi app is handy for a below-grade level you rarely visit, but confirm the front-panel controls still work if the network is down.
products.bestFor: Basements where the drain sits above the machine.
pros: Built-in pump with vertical or horizontal drain
cons: Pump is an extra wear part

buyingCriteria.explanation: ARLIME prints 60 pints at 95F and 90 percent humidity and a lower 45 pints for a milder test. Ludatido's 80 pint figure is a peak. The 2019 US test is 65F and 60 percent, so a 60 pint label can be a 40 pint machine in a cool room. As a rule, size a machine for the wettest month of the year, not the average, because the load peaks when the ground is saturated and the air is warm.

A 60 pint class machine can fill a small bucket in under a day. Ludatido's 1.72 gallon tank and ARLIME's 6.5 liters help. Without a hose, buy the larger tank. If you cannot get to the machine daily, the choice is between a hose, a pump or a very large tank, and the hose is the cheapest option.

A gravity hose needs the drain below the unit. The Midea has a pump that lifts water vertically. If the drain is nearby and low, the Frigidaire or WATTSMART hose options are enough. In a living space, check the low-speed figure and then check owner feedback on the high-speed sound, because machines this size can be loud at full speed.

Ludatido lists 42 dB minimum. Many others publish nothing. Every 10 dB sounds about twice as loud, so a low-mode figure matters for finished space. A square footage claim says nothing about ceiling height, so multiply by height if your basement ceiling is tall.

WATTSMART claims 6,500 sq ft and GarveeLife 3,000. Claims assume a mild moisture problem, so a wet level needs one size up. Verify that the humidistat has a range down to at least 40 percent, because many stop at 35 or 30 and cannot hold a higher target without cycling.

A machine this size draws roughly 600 to 900 watts while running. Energy Star on the GarveeLife keeps running cost in check over a damp season. Add a hygrometer to your shopping list, because it costs little and lets you see if the machine is truly holding the target.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rating honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: We preferred listings that print a milder figure beside the peak. ARLIME scored highest because it names both. That makes it easy to size the machine to the room.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drainage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tank size, hose and pump options across the lineup. A large tank is only useful when you cannot use a hose.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise
howWeEvaluated.description: We read decibel claims, such as Ludatido at 42 dB. Low-mode noise is the most useful decibel figure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Coverage realism
howWeEvaluated.description: We discounted large square footage claims when the pint figure was a maximum. Large claims were treated with caution unless the rating supported them.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered brand reach, filters and owner feedback patterns. Filters and service decide long-term cost.

cards.label: Honest rating
cards.text: ARLIME shows 60 and 45 pints. You can plan around the lower number.

cards.label: Peak rating
cards.text: Ludatido and GarveeLife list maximums. Treat them as best-case.

howToChoose.note: Pick the unit that prints a second number.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A rating you can trust, a drain route and a quiet low setting. Place it centrally.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Frigidaire and Ludatido are the sturdy choices; the Midea fits when the drain is high.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The drain is high or you want brand support. The Midea and Frigidaire earn it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The space is medium and mild. The GarveeLife covers it.

maintenance.why: A blocked filter frosts the coil.

maintenance.task: Check the hose or pump line

faq.q: Is 60 pints too much for a basement?
faq.a: Only for a small one. For a large open level it is appropriate. A smaller room will short-cycle. A 60 pint class unit also draws more power, so factor in running cost.

faq.q: How much does a 60 pint dehumidifier cost?
faq.a: Prices range from a low tier to a premium tier. Check the listing. Prices move, so check the listing before buying.
Only if the drain is above the unit. Cleaning the filter and coil is the best life extension.
Compressor units last 5 to 10 years. Always plan around the lower of two figures when a seller gives both.

faq.q: Why do some listings say 80 pints?
faq.a: Sellers quote a hot-lab peak. Plan around the honest number. A cold basement reduces output on every compressor model.
Aim for 40 to 50 percent. Hold the target even on cool nights.
